newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blue chips dip but end off lows ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blue chips dip but end off lows ahead of data.

text.p: U.S. blue chips extended their decline on Thursday but battered technology and financial stocks showed signs of life as Wall Street braced for a key piece of economic data.
The Dow industrials finished off about 40 points, or 0.6 percent, at 6477. But blue chips rallied late in the day after being down more than 95 points.
All eyes were on Friday's report on March U.S. payrolls, wages and unemployment. "It could be a killer if it goes the wrong way," said Jim Benning, a trader at BT Brokerage.

If the report shows a more robust-than-expected U.S. economy, it will add to growing fears among investors that the Federal Reserve will have to further raise interest rates in order to cool the economy, analysts said.
"It appears that the market's already anticipating a number that's going to cause further indigestion," said Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management.
A Reuter poll of economists produced a consensus forecast of an increase of 196,000 jobs in March. The data is due at 0830 EST/1330 GMT, an hour before the stock market opening.

With the day's losses, the Dow has shed more than 400 points since its steep downturn began last Thursday. The closely watched gauge of 30 stocks has fallen 8.6 percent since its record closing high of 7085 on March 11, and has approached the year's starting point of 6448.
Losing issues outpaced gainers by a 15 to nine ratio on the New York Stock Exchange.

But while blue chips floundered, the groups of stocks that had led the downturn found some buyers on Thursday. Reflecting the bounce in high-technology shares, the Nasdaq composite rose almost 13 points, or one percent, to 1214.
Before Thursday's session the Nasdaq index had fallen 13.5 percent from its peak closing level set January 22.
Among leading tech issues, Intel Corp rose 3-5/8 to 140-5/8, Microsoft Corp gained 3-1/8 to 95-1/8 and Oracle Corp added 1-7/8 to 38-5/8.
Battered financial stocks also attracted buyers. Morgan Stanley Group Inc jumped 2-3/8 to 59-7/8, Citicorp advanced 1-3/4 to 111-5/8 and BankAmerica Corp added one to 101-1/8.
Despite the rebound in some sectors, market watchers said further selling could be in store for Wall Street.

James Melcher, president of Balestra Capital, said he has moved to 50 percent cash, the first time at that level since shortly before the 1987 stock market crash. He said would not be surprised to see the Dow drop "a couple of thousand points" as money flowing into equity mutual funds dries up.
"I don't know how many more days of this people can take before they think it might be prudent to move a little bit of money out of their equity mutual fund into their money market fund," he said.

International Business Machines Corp did not take part in the tech-stock rebound. Shares in the computer giant tumbled 2-5/8 to 131-1/8 on renewed fears that currency translations and a mainframe product transition will hurt its first quarter earnings. A Wall Street Journal column highlighted recent actions by analysts who cut their IBM earnings estimates.
Lucent Technologies Inc shares jumped 1-3/4 to 52 after the company told analysts it has cut internal costs and expects strong second-quarter sales in its software and wireless divisions.

Pharmaceutical company Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc fell 2-3/4 to 69-3/4 after a Salomon Brothers analyst downgraded his rating on the stock to hold from strong buy and cut his 1997 earnings per share forecast on the company.
Microchip Technology Inc gained 1-13/16 to 31-1/8 after saying it expects its revenues and earnings for its fourth fiscal quarter, ended March 31, to reach record levels.
The S&P 500 index rose 0.21 points to 750.32.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 12.76 points to 1213.76.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
